title: Understanding AI
why: Recognize what AI can do, where it helps, and why human judgment still matters.

concepts.title: Artificial intelligence
concepts.point: Software can recognize patterns, predict outcomes, and generate content.
concepts.visual: Three familiar objects: photo, weather forecast, draft letter.

concepts.title: Machine learning
concepts.point: Learn patterns from examples instead of writing every rule.
concepts.visual: Fruit sorter learning from labeled examples.

concepts.title: Generative AI
concepts.point: Create new content using learned patterns and supplied instructions.
concepts.visual: One brief becoming text, image, and audio waveform.

concepts.title: Model versus application
concepts.point: The model is one component of a usable product.
concepts.visual: Engine beside complete car; reuse pilot 004.

concepts.title: Prediction versus generation
concepts.point: Estimating an outcome differs from creating content.
concepts.visual: Forecast demand versus draft tomorrow's menu.

concepts.title: Multimodal AI
concepts.point: Work with different types of information together.
concepts.visual: Photo, voice note, and written question in one workspace.

concepts.title: Hallucination
concepts.point: A convincing answer can still be wrong or unsupported.
concepts.visual: Polished answer with one unsupported claim highlighted for checking.

concepts.title: Human augmentation
concepts.point: Decide what AI handles and what a person judges.
concepts.visual: Navigation assistant suggests route; human drives.

title: Understanding data
why: Understand the information behind AI so you can spot weak inputs and misleading conclusions.

concepts.title: Structured and unstructured data
concepts.point: Information comes in organized fields and freer forms.
concepts.visual: Spreadsheet beside emails, photographs, recordings.

concepts.title: Data quality
concepts.point: Missing, stale, or incorrect inputs weaken results.
concepts.visual: Recipe with missing quantity and expired ingredient.

concepts.title: Features and labels
concepts.point: Features describe examples; labels provide known answers.
concepts.visual: Fruit card with size and color beside fruit name.

concepts.title: Sampling bias
concepts.point: A narrow sample can give a misleading picture.
concepts.visual: Inspecting only the top layer of a varied fruit basket.

concepts.title: Privacy and consent
concepts.point: Having access does not mean every use is permitted.
concepts.visual: Personal file with clear purpose and permission boundaries.

concepts.title: Probability and uncertainty
concepts.point: Likelihood is different from certainty.
concepts.visual: Forecast with several possible outcomes; no unsupported percentages.

concepts.title: Correlation versus causation
concepts.point: Moving together does not prove one thing causes another.
concepts.visual: Hot weather influences both ice-cream sales and swimming.

concepts.title: Data visualization
concepts.point: Choose a view that answers a specific question.
concepts.visual: Small illustrative table beside clear matching chart.

title: How machines learn
why: Understand learning and testing so you can distinguish genuine improvement from memorization.

concepts.title: Supervised learning
concepts.point: Learn from examples paired with known answers.
concepts.visual: Practice cards paired with answers.

concepts.title: Unsupervised learning
concepts.point: Find groups or patterns without supplied answer labels.
concepts.visual: Unlabeled objects arranged into similar groups.

concepts.title: Reinforcement learning
concepts.point: Learn behavior from actions and reward signals.
concepts.visual: Simple maze with feedback along attempted routes.

concepts.title: Neural networks and deep learning
concepts.point: Layers of learned transformations build useful representations.
concepts.visual: Image through a few clearly simplified processing layers; no biological brain claim.

concepts.title: Training versus inference
concepts.point: Training updates the model; inference uses it.
concepts.visual: Cooking practice versus serving a dish; reuse pilot 021.

concepts.title: Training, validation, and test sets
concepts.point: Practice, tune, then assess on held-out examples.
concepts.visual: Three separate stacks: practice, validation, test.

concepts.title: Overfitting
concepts.point: Memorizing examples can fail on unfamiliar cases.
concepts.visual: Learner masters one exact route but struggles at detour.

concepts.title: Fine-tuning
concepts.point: Additional training adapts model behavior for a task.
concepts.visual: Generally trained cook receiving specialist pastry training.

title: Generative AI and prompting
why: Understand generation and give clear instructions that produce useful, checkable results.

concepts.title: Large language models
concepts.point: Language models generate text by modeling token sequences.
concepts.visual: Sentence extending a small piece at a time.

concepts.title: Tokens
concepts.point: Text is processed in pieces that are not always whole words.
concepts.visual: Short sentence divided into illustrative variable-sized tiles; label illustrative tokenization.

concepts.title: Context window
concepts.point: Each interaction has a bounded working space.
concepts.visual: Desk with limited room for relevant pages.

concepts.title: Attention
concepts.point: Weight relationships between parts of the input.
concepts.visual: Pronoun linked to the words that clarify it; no human attention claim.

concepts.title: Diffusion
concepts.point: A diffusion process gradually transforms noise into an image.
concepts.visual: Noise, emerging structure, finished object; avoid claiming all image models work this way.

concepts.title: A clear prompt
concepts.point: Specify the task, context, constraints, and desired result.
concepts.visual: Precise restaurant order versus ambiguous request.

concepts.title: Few-shot prompting
concepts.point: Examples demonstrate the pattern you want.
concepts.visual: Two completed examples followed by new matching task.

concepts.title: Output contracts
concepts.point: Define the answer's shape before using it downstream.
concepts.visual: Free-form text beside a clearly labeled output template.

concepts.title: Task decomposition
concepts.point: Break a complex request into manageable parts.
concepts.visual: Shopping, preparation, cooking as three meal-planning steps.

concepts.title: Verification
concepts.point: Check claims and results against evidence or tests.
concepts.visual: Draft checked against source, calculation, and requirements.

title: Context, knowledge, and memory
why: Give AI the right information at the right time instead of relying on longer prompts alone.

concepts.title: Context engineering
concepts.point: Select information needed for the next step.
concepts.visual: Chef's station with only relevant recipe, ingredients, and tools.

concepts.title: Grounding
concepts.point: Connect an answer to supplied evidence.
concepts.visual: Answer statements connected to highlighted source passages.

concepts.title: Embeddings
concepts.point: Represent items numerically to compare useful similarities.
concepts.visual: Illustrative semantic map with related phrases near each other.

concepts.title: Semantic search
concepts.point: Search by meaning, beyond exact word overlap.
concepts.visual: Vehicle repair query finds Fixing your car document.

concepts.title: Chunking
concepts.point: Split material into useful retrieval units.
concepts.visual: Manual divided at meaningful section boundaries.

concepts.title: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
concepts.point: Retrieve evidence, add context, then generate.
concepts.visual: Three-stage process; reuse pilot 040.

concepts.title: Persistent memory
concepts.point: Store selected information for later interactions.
concepts.visual: Temporary desk beside durable notebook; no automatic model retraining.

concepts.title: RAG versus fine-tuning
concepts.point: Supplying reference material differs from changing model parameters.
concepts.visual: Open reference book beside specialist training.

title: Technology building blocks
why: Understand how AI connects to software and becomes a working application.

concepts.title: APIs
concepts.point: Software interacts through defined interfaces.
concepts.visual: Service counter exchanging request and result.

concepts.title: JSON and schemas
concepts.point: Structured fields support reliable exchange and validation.
concepts.visual: Delivery label with required name, address, and item fields.

concepts.title: Databases and queries
concepts.point: Store records and retrieve what you need.
concepts.visual: Organized cabinet with precise lookup request.

concepts.title: Webhooks
concepts.point: An event can notify another system automatically.
concepts.visual: Doorbell signals arrival rather than repeated door checks.

concepts.title: Authentication and authorization
concepts.point: Identity and permission answer different questions.
concepts.visual: Identity badge beside door-access list.

concepts.title: Frontend and backend
concepts.point: Visible interface and underlying processing work together.
concepts.visual: Restaurant dining room and kitchen.

concepts.title: Version control
concepts.point: Track changes and recover earlier versions.
concepts.visual: Document timeline with named checkpoints.

concepts.title: Deployment
concepts.point: Make a tested application available in its intended environment.
concepts.visual: Prototype becomes a maintained service.

title: Reusable capabilities and workflows
why: Turn one-off tasks into repeatable processes and reusable capabilities.

concepts.title: Workflow mapping
concepts.point: Make inputs, steps, decisions, and outputs explicit.
concepts.visual: Simple order-to-delivery process.

concepts.title: Triggers and conditions
concepts.point: Define when work starts and which rules apply.
concepts.visual: Incoming request at one clear decision gate.

concepts.title: Prompt chaining
concepts.point: One step supplies input to the next.
concepts.visual: Research, outline, draft as three stations.

concepts.title: Routing
concepts.point: Send a task to an appropriate path.
concepts.visual: Reception desk directs requests to specialists.

concepts.title: Parallel execution
concepts.point: Independent tasks can run simultaneously.
concepts.visual: Cooks preparing separate dishes at once.

concepts.title: Reusable templates
concepts.point: Parameterize recurring instructions rather than rewrite them.
concepts.visual: Report template filled with different client details.

concepts.title: Agent skills
concepts.point: Package instructions, resources, and scripts for recurring work.
concepts.visual: Task kit containing guide, tools, and examples.

concepts.title: Project workspaces
concepts.point: Keep relevant instructions and reference material together.
concepts.visual: Separate project folders with their own materials.

title: Agents and agentic systems
why: Understand how agents select actions, use tools, and coordinate within boundaries.

concepts.title: AI agents
concepts.point: Select actions toward a goal within defined boundaries.
concepts.visual: Fixed recipe versus cook adapting next step to conditions.

concepts.title: Agent loop
concepts.point: Use results to decide whether to continue or stop.
concepts.visual: Observe, decide, act loop with exit; reuse pilot 060.

concepts.title: Planning and replanning
concepts.point: Revise steps when conditions change.
concepts.visual: Route updated after road closure.

concepts.title: Tool calling
concepts.point: A model requests an action that software executes.
concepts.visual: Assistant selecting calculator, search, or calendar.

concepts.title: Agent harness
concepts.point: Surrounding software manages execution, tools, and limits.
concepts.visual: Model inside a labeled operating frame; scope varies by implementation.

concepts.title: State and checkpoints
concepts.point: Track progress so work can resume or recover.
concepts.visual: Task board with saved checkpoint.

concepts.title: Multi-agent orchestration
concepts.point: Divide work when benefits justify coordination costs.
concepts.visual: Coordinator assigning distinct roles to small team.

concepts.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP)
concepts.point: Standardize connections to tools and context.
concepts.visual: Host with client connections to capability-providing servers; not automatic security.

concepts.title: Agent-to-agent communication
concepts.point: Exchange tasks and results across agent systems.
concepts.visual: Service desks exchanging task ticket and deliverable.

concepts.title: Computer-use agents
concepts.point: Interact with software through its interface.
concepts.visual: Agent uses browser within action boundaries and checkpoints.

title: Quality, safety, and reliability
why: Test and monitor systems before trusting them with consequential work.

concepts.title: Evaluations
concepts.point: Test representative tasks against explicit success criteria.
concepts.visual: Driving test under several conditions, not one easy road.

concepts.title: Precision and recall
concepts.point: False alarms and missed cases are different errors.
concepts.visual: Sorting tray shows correct selections, wrong selections, and missed items; formulas only if accurate.

concepts.title: RAG evaluation
concepts.point: Assess retrieval and answer support separately.
concepts.visual: Found the right passage? versus Used it correctly?

concepts.title: Guardrails
concepts.point: Checks constrain behavior but do not guarantee safety or correctness.
concepts.visual: Multiple inspection points around workflow.

concepts.title: Prompt injection
concepts.point: Untrusted content may attempt to redirect the system.
concepts.visual: Retrieved document with a suspicious instruction clearly distinguished from user task.

concepts.title: Least privilege and human approval
concepts.point: Grant necessary access and review consequential actions.
concepts.visual: Restricted keyring beside human approval gate.

concepts.title: Tracing and observability
concepts.point: Record events so failures can be investigated.
concepts.visual: Task timeline of model calls and tools with failed step.

concepts.title: Quality, latency, and cost
concepts.point: Evaluate tradeoffs against the task's needs.
concepts.visual: Three labeled controls and task-specific target; no invented benchmarks.

title: AI across workplace functions
why: Recognize useful AI patterns across professions and connect learning to real work.

concepts.title: Document workflows
concepts.point: Transform source material into a reviewable deliverable.
concepts.visual: Meeting notes become structured brief with sources.

concepts.title: Data-analysis workflows
concepts.point: Move from question to checked calculation and explanation.
concepts.visual: Question, small spreadsheet, verified result.

concepts.title: Decision dashboards
concepts.point: Connect measures to actions people can take.
concepts.visual: One clear indicator linked to one decision; illustrative data.

concepts.title: Multimedia production workflows
concepts.point: Coordinate brief, assets, editing, and review.
concepts.visual: One brief becomes coordinated image, audio, video set.

concepts.title: HR and recruitment support
concepts.point: Assist administration while preserving human hiring decisions.
concepts.visual: Scheduling and document preparation around human-led process.

concepts.title: Finance exception handling
concepts.point: Flag discrepancies for investigation.
concepts.visual: Invoices through matching checks with one flagged discrepancy.

concepts.title: Operations and project coordination
concepts.point: Route work, track dependencies, and escalate blockers.
concepts.visual: Task board with one visible bottleneck.

concepts.title: AI-assisted software delivery
concepts.point: Build from requirements through testing and deployment.
concepts.visual: Company website through four checked stages.

title: Business value and monetization
why: Connect technical capability to customer problems, delivery costs, and clear offers.

concepts.title: Customer discovery
concepts.point: Understand the problem before choosing technology.
concepts.visual: Founder listens to customer before opening toolbox.

concepts.title: Use-case prioritization
concepts.point: Compare expected value, feasibility, and risk.
concepts.visual: Three candidate tasks on simple qualitative scorecard.

concepts.title: Minimum viable product
concepts.point: Test an outcome with the smallest credible solution.
concepts.visual: One working service counter before full store.

concepts.title: Value proposition
concepts.point: Explain customer outcomes rather than just AI features.
concepts.visual: Feature-heavy description becomes clear benefit.

concepts.title: Lead-generation workflows
concepts.point: Research prospects and prepare relevant, reviewable outreach.
concepts.visual: Research, qualification, draft, human review.

concepts.title: Sales and CRM workflows
concepts.point: Maintain continuity from inquiry to follow-up.
concepts.visual: Customer record moving through meaningful stages.

concepts.title: Unit economics
concepts.point: Revenue less variable costs gives contribution, not net profit.
concepts.visual: Illustrative $100 minus $40 equals $60 before fixed costs and taxes; reuse pilot 091.

concepts.title: Productized services
concepts.point: Package a repeatable outcome with defined scope.
concepts.visual: Loose skills become a clear service offering.

title: Leadership, mindset, and future skills
why: Lead adoption with judgment, accountability, and skills that transfer as tools change.

concepts.title: Systems thinking
concepts.point: Improving one step may not improve the whole process.
concepts.visual: Fast workstation feeding a slower bottleneck.

concepts.title: Critical judgment
concepts.point: Question assumptions and seek evidence.
concepts.visual: Decision card with evidence, assumptions, uncertainties.

concepts.title: Effective delegation
concepts.point: Specify outcomes, boundaries, and review points.
concepts.visual: Clear task brief; reuse pilot 095.

concepts.title: Change management
concepts.point: Adoption needs redesigned work, training, and support.
concepts.visual: Team moves from old process to supported new process.

concepts.title: Accountability and governance
concepts.point: Assign owners for decisions, access, and failures.
concepts.visual: Workflow with visible human owners.

concepts.title: Feedback loops
concepts.point: Use measured results to decide what to improve.
concepts.visual: Build, measure, review, revise loop.

concepts.title: Learning agility
concepts.point: Practice skills that transfer as tools change.
concepts.visual: Stable foundation supporting replaceable tools.

concepts.title: Future readiness
concepts.point: Prepare for plausible scenarios rather than certain forecasts.
concepts.visual: Several possible paths supported by data, judgment, and communication.
